question: Should OpenClaw core accept opt-in agent self-continuation and model-directed delegate returns now, including the default-disabled cross-session targeting policy?
rationale: This is not a routine bug fix: it adds a core agent capability, config surface, state model, and security/session boundary whose permanent product shape needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Stage guarded core merge after cleanup
options.body: Resolve conflicts, fix the remaining status-text row, keep the feature disabled by default, and land only after exact-head upgrade/security proof is attached.

options.title: Accept as experimental core capability
options.body: Maintain the current broad branch shape and explicitly own the compatibility and security-boundary risks as an experimental opt-in feature.

options.title: Pause core merge
options.body: Close or pause this PR if maintainers want continuation to incubate outside core until a narrower API and rollout plan exists.

recommendation.title: Stage guarded core merge after cleanup
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts, fix the remaining status-text row, keep the feature disabled by default, and land only after exact-head upgrade/security proof is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed the continuation shape and explicitly identified crossSessionTargeting as a maintainer-deferred choice.
